corrections.critique: Strongest feature: Malpass precisely distinguishes finite proper-part intuitions from infinite equinumerosity, using the even and natural numbers to show why counterintuitive one-to-one correspondence does not logically establish metaphysical impossibility. Principal limitation: Mathematical consistency alone cannot determine whether concretely instantiated infinities are metaphysically possible, so the reply appropriately blocks Craig's inference without independently demonstrating their actuality. Live burden: The defender must supply a non-question-begging metaphysical principle explaining why proper-subset equinumerosity is impossible in reality, rather than merely importing finite-domain expectations into the disputed infinite context. Locked score: The 92 accurately reflects a decisive, highly responsive diagnostic defeat with stable terminology, explicit qualification, strong charity, and sufficient warrant, while preserving the limited conclusion that Craig's illustration fails to prove impossibility.
